title: Protesters march in Madrid against gender-based violence

tea.why: Protesters marched to oppose gender-based violence and express concern over potential rollbacks of women's rights ahead of general elections.
tea.want: They demanded that the fight against gender-based violence remain a priority for political parties and opposed the repeal of protection laws.
tea.changed: Nov 25: Thousands marched in Madrid in two separate demonstrations to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

summary: On November 25, 2026, thousands of people participated in two separate marches in Madrid to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Organised by the Foro de Madrid, the Movimiento Feminista, and the Comisión 8M, the demonstrations aimed to protest against gender-based violence and warn against a potential regression in women's rights ahead of the upcoming general elections. Participants expressed concern over political rhetoric questioning existing protections against gender violence. While the marches were peaceful, they highlighted divisions within the feminist movement regarding strategy. Authorities and organisers provided differing estimates on the number of attendees for both events. Similar demonstrations took place in other Spanish cities, including Barcelona, as part of a broader national effort to keep gender violence on the political agenda.
demands: Prioritise the fight against gender-based violence
Oppose the repeal of gender violence laws
response: The Spanish government condemned the trivialisation of gender-based violence, while the political party Vox has advocated for the repeal of the 2004 law against gender-based violence, arguing it criminalises men.
